oneVisit: complete one route segment, one active incident, or one relationship scene
continuity: persistent personal journey plus versioned shared roads
playerRole: an ordinary traveler carrying a letter signed by their future self
coreQuestion: What must be preserved so people can still reach one another after the roads fail?
worldRules: A years-long storm damaged roads and communications but did not end ordinary life.
The player may choose the order of regions and may ignore the main mystery for long periods.
A rare atmospheric event at the far white tower can send one physical letter three years backward.
Shared-world changes affect public routes and landmarks, never private relationships or endings directly.
Every visible option must be grounded in the current scene or authoritative known state.

regions.role: starting coast and damaged postal network
wide routes, farms, markets, and migrating communities
dense paths, ferries, hidden settlements, and intimate character stories
rail towns, workshops, scarce transport, and labor conflicts
long sightlines, seasonal rivers, observatories, and route planning
snow passes, tunnels, isolation, and late-game risk
lighthouses, tide post, the white tower, and final choices

mainMystery.incitingLetter: Do not take the shortest road. Find the people who never received a reply. Bring their names to the white tower.
mainMystery.truth: The white tower can send one letter backward during a rare storm alignment; the future player used it after seeing which communities disappeared when the restored network favored speed over access.
finalDecisions: send the original warning and preserve the loop
send a different letter that changes the player's own journey
end backward delivery and convert the tower into an open relay
leave the mechanism unused and preserve only the human road network

safetyBoundaries: No private relationship, secret, free-text action, or unrevealed quest becomes public.
No single player free-text input creates a permanent shared place or rule.
No main ending requires multiplayer participation.
Failed generation never rolls back a committed shared action.
